acceptance_criteria.criterion: constraints.md contains a rule under the Testing section prohibiting implicit floating-point format strings and requiring FormattableString.Invariant or CultureInfo.InvariantCulture.
The rule includes the rationale (non-English locale decimal-separator issue causing 1 000× parsing error).

summary: Added culture-invariant floating-point format string rule to the Testing section of constraints.md (line 152).
Rule prohibits implicit float/double format strings in tests that are subsequently parsed back, and mandates FormattableString.Invariant(...) or .ToString("Fx", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture) instead.
Rationale is included: non-English decimal separator (comma) causes a dot-expecting parser to silently discard fractional digits, producing a value ~1000× too small.

comments.note: Rule wording includes both the mandatory forms (FormattableString.Invariant and .ToString with CultureInfo.InvariantCulture) and a concrete counter-example ('1.5' → '1,5' → silently parsed as 0.0015) making the rationale immediately understandable to future readers.
